request.state: Incident review notes, week 41. On Monday the payments team deployed version 4.12 of the checkout service, which introduced a new retry policy for card authorisations. By Tuesday morning the support queue showed a sharp rise in tickets from customers in three European regions reporting that the pay button spun forever and then displayed a generic error. Engineers traced the problem to a connection pool that was sized for the old retry policy: each failed authorisation now held a connection for up to thirty seconds, and under normal evening load the pool was exhausted within minutes. While the pool was exhausted, unrelated requests such as cart updates and address lookups also timed out, which is why some customers believed the whole shop was down. The on-call engineer rolled the service back at 18:40 and error rates returned to baseline within ten minutes. Finance has asked whether any customers were charged twice; the preliminary answer is that eleven authorisations were captured twice because the retry fired after a slow success response, and those charges have already been reversed. A customer named Maria Lopez wrote in to say she had been charged twice for order 88213 and wants a refund by Friday, otherwise she will dispute the charge with her bank. The account manager for the enterprise customer Northwind Traders also asked whether the incident affects their service level agreement, since their nightly batch of roughly four thousand orders failed on Tuesday and had to be resubmitted manually on Wednesday. Product management would like a summary of customer impact, the root cause and the remediation plan before the Thursday review. The remediation plan includes sizing the pool independently per dependency, adding a circuit breaker around the authorisation provider, a load test that replays Tuesday evening traffic, and an alert on pool saturation above eighty percent. None of these items has an owner yet, and the post-incident review has not been scheduled.
